editorial:
Imagine waking up and finding out your favorite artist never existed. That is exactly what happens to Fabrice, a boring office worker who lives for the music of French rock star Johnny Hallyday. His life is pretty dull until he slips into a parallel world where Johnny never recorded a single song. It is a wild and funny setup that explores how much our favorite music defines who we are. You will feel for Fabrice as he tries to navigate a world that feels completely wrong, all while dealing with his monotonous job and a society that doesn't understand his passion.

The acting is great and the comedy hits well, especially when Fabrice tries to explain the music that should exist. The pacing is quick, though some of the smaller plot points might feel a bit random. If you enjoy quirky comedies with a supernatural twist, you will love this. Since it is an older film, you might want to look for a high-quality digital version. I suggest streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best experience, or you can rent it on Apple TV if you just want a quick movie night with friends.
endingExplained: In the end, Fabrice realizes that his obsession with the singer was a way to avoid his own real-life problems. After a series of crazy events in the alternate world, he finally finds a way to return to his own reality. He wakes up back in his original universe where Johnny Hallyday is still a star. Instead of going back to his boring routine, he decides to actually live his life and change his habits.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves weird parallel universe stories and music.
